<ExternalIntegrationHeader integration={{"name":"Mopidy","description":"Control your Mopidy servers: music, volume, playlists, web radios, search, notifications.","owner":"guim31","owner_avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/33096540?v=4","repo_url":"https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mopidy","cover_url":"https://integration-store-storage.gladysassistant.com/covers/guim31--gladys-mopidy.png","type":"device","version":"1.1.1","gladys_version":">=5.3.0","stars":0,"pushed_at":"2026-10-25T19:17:58Z"}} />

Control your [Mopidy](https://mopidy.com) music servers from Gladys: local
files, web radios, and every source a Mopidy extension adds (Jellyfin,
YouTube Music, TuneIn, Subsonic…). Play, pause, change the track, the volume
and the mute, start a playlist or a search, play a doorbell sound or a web
radio and then go back to the music, see what is playing on the dashboard.
Everything stays on your local network: no cloud, no account.

The integration talks to Mopidy through its native API (Mopidy-HTTP: JSON-RPC
and the event WebSocket), so it sees changes the instant they happen and knows
the Mopidy URIs. It was tested against real Mopidy servers, **Mopidy 3.4.2**
(Debian package) and **4.0.5**. If your Mopidy only exposes MPD
(Mopidy-MPD), use the [gladys-mpd](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mpd)
integration instead. Feedback welcome in the
[issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mopidy/issues).

This integration is not affiliated with the Mopidy project.

## What you need

- Gladys Assistant **5.3.0** or later.
- Mopidy 3 or 4 with its HTTP frontend (**Mopidy-HTTP**, enabled by default),
  reachable from Gladys on the network: in `mopidy.conf`, section `[http]`,
  set `hostname = 0.0.0.0` (the default `127.0.0.1` only answers the machine
  itself). The port is **6680** by default.
- Mopidy-HTTP has no password: keep it on your home network. A Mopidy behind
  a reverse proxy in HTTPS works too (enter `https://…`), as long as the proxy
  asks Gladys for no password.

## Set up

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**, then **Install from GitHub**, and enter
   `https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mopidy` (or install **Mopidy** from the
   catalog once it is listed).
2. In **Configuration**, enter the address of your server (`192.168.1.20`,
   `mopidy.home`, `192.168.1.20:6681` for another port, or the address of
   its web client copied from the browser, `http://192.168.1.20:6680/iris/`)
   and a name (`Living room`). Up to three more servers below.
3. Choose the **Language of the devices** (names of the features, messages)
   and, if you want, the **Notification volume**. Save.
4. Click **Test the connection**: one line per server, with the Mopidy
   version, what it is doing, its volume and its playlists.
5. Open the **Discover** tab and add the devices.

Use fixed IP addresses (a DHCP reservation in your router) or names your DNS
resolves: names ending in `.local` do not resolve inside the integration
container.

## The device of each server

Each Mopidy server is one device. Gladys shows it as a music player: the
**Music** dashboard box and the **Talk on a speaker** and **Play music on a
speaker** scene actions work with it (see the next section).

| Feature (English names) | What it does                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Play                    | Plays the queue (a paused track resumes where it was).                                                                                              |
| Pause                   | Pauses.                                                                                                                                             |
| Previous track          | Goes to the previous track.                                                                                                                         |
| Next track              | Goes to the next track.                                                                                                                             |
| Volume                  | 0 to 100 %, as Mopidy sees it. Absent when Mopidy has no mixer (`mixer = none`).                                                                    |
| Mute                    | On or off: the mute of Mopidy's mixer.                                                                                                              |
| Playback state          | 1 playing, 0 paused, 2 stopped. Writable: Gladys plays, pauses and stops through it. Usable as a scene trigger or condition.                        |
| Title                   | Title of the track, or the song a web radio announces. Empty when nothing is loaded.                                                                |
| Artist                  | Artist(s) of the track.                                                                                                                             |
| Album                   | Album of the track, or the station of a web radio.                                                                                                  |
| Artwork                 | Cover of the track, shown by the **Music** box (see Limits).                                                                                        |
| Duration                | Length of the track in seconds, 0 for a web radio.                                                                                                  |
| Position                | Position in the track in seconds; changing it seeks. Sent on a change of track or state and on a seek: Gladys moves the bar on its own.             |
| Shuffle                 | Random play of Mopidy.                                                                                                                              |
| Repeat                  | Off, the whole queue, or the current track.                                                                                                         |
| Now playing             | "Title — Artist", "Paused · …" or "Stopped". For a web radio, the song it announces. From version 1.0, kept for the dashboards and scenes using it. |
| Playlist                | A list of the Mopidy playlists: picking one replaces the queue with it and plays it.                                                                |
| Notification            | Receives an address to play, then puts back what was playing (see below).                                                                           |

The list of playlists follows Mopidy: a playlist created or deleted appears
or disappears in the list.

## Gladys 5.3 music player

Since Gladys 5.3, the **Music** box of the dashboard is a real player, and
Mopidy fills all of it:

- the cover, the title, the artist and the album, a progress bar you can drag
  to seek, play and pause, previous, next, shuffle, repeat, the volume and the
  mute;
- the **queue** (list button): the tracks of the Mopidy queue, the current one
  highlighted; a tap plays another one;
- **search and browse** (magnifier button): the search asks every Mopidy
  backend that searches (artists, albums, tracks) and looks in the names of
  the playlists; browsing starts with **Playlists**, then the folders of
  Mopidy (**Files**, **Local media** with Mopidy-Local, those of your other
  extensions). A tap plays the item in place of the queue; the secondary
  gesture adds it after the current track or at the end of the queue. A
  folder opens, it does not play.

The **Play music on a speaker** scene action of Gladys picks a playlist, an
album or a track in the same panel, and plays it when the scene runs.

**A device added before version 1.1.0** keeps working as before, without the
new features: open the **Discover** tab of the integration and click
**Update** on the server (Gladys offers it because the features changed). The
new features are added; the existing ones keep their scenes and dashboards.
Two of them change: **Mute** becomes a music mute (it was a switch), and
**Playback state** reads 2 instead of 0 when Mopidy is stopped.

Covers come from Mopidy: Mopidy-Local gives the cover file of the album
folder or the cover embedded in the files, other extensions their own. Gladys
shows a cover of **300 KB at most**, and Mopidy-Local serves the file as it is
on disk: the integration makes a larger cover smaller (a JPEG of 400 pixels at
most), up to 10 MB (see Limits).

## Dashboard widget

Add the **Mopidy player** widget to a dashboard. In its settings, pick a
server (empty: the first one of the configuration). It shows:

- the **title** of the track and, below, the artist and the album (or the
  station of a web radio);
- the **volume** as a gauge;
- the state (playing, paused, stopped), the position in the queue, random and
  repeat;
- four buttons: **Previous**, **Play** or **Pause**, **Next** and
  **Options…**. Options… opens a form filled with the current values: the
  volume, a playlist to play, random play and repeat. Only what you change is
  sent.

The widget follows the server as it changes: it is refreshed within ten
seconds when a track starts, the volume moves or a playlist is created. The **Music** box of Gladys 5.3 (above) is the full player; this widget adds the **Options…** form and has no cover.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Mopidy track started**: Mopidy starts a track — play, next track, a
  playlist, another client such as Iris or a phone app. Optionally limited to
  one server. The scene gets the title, the artist, the album, the URI of the
  track, and "artist · album". Notifications do not trigger it, nor the track
  resumed after one.
- **Mopidy server lost**: a server that answered stops answering (switched
  off, crashed, off the network). Optionally limited to one server; the scene
  gets its name.

Whether music plays or not is the **Playback state** feature: use the core
trigger on a device state for that.

### Actions

The server is chosen among the devices of the integration (empty: the first
one of the configuration).

- **Play a Mopidy playlist**: replaces the queue with a Mopidy playlist, by its
  name (capitals and accents do not matter) or its URI, and plays it. The
  number of tracks queued can be used in the next actions of the scene. An
  unknown name fails the action with the list of the playlists. You can also
  choose a playlist from a list with the core action **Control a device**, on
  the **Playlist** feature.
- **Play an address on Mopidy**: plays an address — a web radio (`http://…`,
  `https://…`), a sound on a web server, or a Mopidy URI (`file:///music/doorbell.ogg`,
  `local:track:…`, `tunein:station:…`) — at the volume you give (empty:
  unchanged). _Then_: **Resume the previous music** (the address plays once,
  then what was playing comes back, see below) or **Keep playing it
  (replaces the queue)**. The action fails when Mopidy cannot play the address.
- **Search and play on Mopidy**: searches the library of Mopidy (every backend
  that can search: local files with Mopidy-Local, Jellyfin, YouTube Music…)
  for an artist, an album or a title, and plays the first 50 tracks found in
  place of the queue. The number of tracks can be used in the next actions.
- **Clear the Mopidy queue**: stops the server and removes every track from
  its queue.
- **Mopidy random play**: on, off, or toggle. The result (on or off) can be
  used in the next actions.
- **Mopidy repeat**: off, the whole queue, or the current track.

### Notifications and "Talk on a speaker"

The **Notification** feature of a server, the **Play an address on Mopidy**
action with _Resume the previous music_, and the **Talk on a speaker** action
of Gladys (the voice comes from Gladys Plus) all work the same way:

1. the address is added at the end of the queue (your queue is never
   replaced) and played at once, with the **Notification volume** of the
   configuration (or the volume of the action);
2. Mopidy stops after it; it is then removed from the queue, and the volume
   and the options (random, repeat, single, consume) come back;
3. the track that was playing resumes at the second it was interrupted; a
   paused track stays paused, a stopped server stays stopped.

A second notification while the first one plays replaces it. If someone takes
over the server meanwhile (another track, the next one), the notification
ends without touching the music. A notification that still plays after five
minutes is ended and the music comes back. A web radio sent as a notification
is not a notification: it keeps playing (its address stays in the queue).

The **Talk on a speaker** action has a volume slider, but Gladys does not pass
it on to external integrations: use the **Notification volume** of the
configuration.

### Scene ideas

- **Morning music**: at 7:00, _Play music on a speaker_ with the **Morning** playlist on the kitchen server.
- **Doorbell**: when the doorbell button is pressed, _Play an address on
  Mopidy_ `file:///music/sounds/doorbell.ogg` on the living room server,
  volume 70, then resume the previous music.
- **Wake-up radio**: at 7:00 on weekdays, _Play an address on Mopidy_ with the
  address of your favorite radio, _Keep playing it_, volume 25; at 7:45, the
  **Pause** feature.
- **Evening**: at sunset, _Search and play on Mopidy_ "jazz", then _Mopidy
  random play_ on.
- **Nobody home**: when the house becomes empty, the **Pause** feature of
  every server.
- **Server down**: on _Mopidy server lost_, send a message to the
  family: the music server of the living room is down.

## How it refreshes

The integration keeps Mopidy's event WebSocket open on each server: what
happens on Mopidy, from Gladys or from another client, is in Gladys within a
second. On top of that, every server is read every 30 seconds (it also checks
that it still answers, and opens the WebSocket again if a proxy dropped it),
and an unchanged value is sent again every six hours so that Gladys never
shows it as old. Only the changes are sent to Gladys.

A server that stops answering is shown unreachable (transport badge of the
device, connection status of the integration), and the integration tries
again: after 2, 5, 15, 30 seconds, then every minute. Nothing else is needed
when it comes back.

Mopidy has no quota: the integration sends one batch of reads per change and
one every 30 seconds per server.

## Troubleshooting

- **"does not answer"**: check the address and the port (6680, or the `port`
  of the `[http]` section of `mopidy.conf`), that Mopidy listens on the
  network (`hostname = 0.0.0.0`) and that no firewall blocks the port between
  Gladys and the server.
- **"no Mopidy-HTTP at this address and port"**: something else answers on
  this port, or Mopidy-HTTP is disabled (`enabled = false` in `[http]`).
- **"access refused (a proxy in front of Mopidy?)"**: a reverse proxy asks for
  a password: let Gladys reach Mopidy directly on port 6680.
- **"no live events" in Test the connection**: the WebSocket `/mopidy/ws`
  cannot be opened (a proxy that does not pass WebSockets): the states are
  then read every 30 seconds.
- **The volume stays empty**: Mopidy has no mixer (`mixer = none` in the
  `[audio]` section, for a fixed-volume output): change the volume on the
  amplifier.
- **A notification does not play**: the address must be reachable from the
  Mopidy server itself (not from Gladys), and known to an installed backend:
  `http(s)://` needs the Stream backend (built in), `file://` a folder of the
  `[file]` section, `tunein:` the TuneIn extension. **No Mopidy extension can
  play this address** means no backend knows its scheme.
- **The Playlist list is empty**: Mopidy has no playlist yet (M3U playlists
  live in `playlists_dir` of the `[m3u]` section).
- **More details**: the logs of the integration (Integrations → Mopidy → Logs)
  show the connections, the losses and the returns, and one line per command.
  Restart the container with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see every event received.

## Limits

- Up to four servers. A server is known by its slot in the configuration:
  changing its address keeps the device and its history.
- Covers above 10 MB or 25 megapixels are not shown, nor covers in another format than JPEG, PNG and WebP (GIF…), nor WebP covers above 300 KB: the integration only reduces JPEG and PNG.
- The search of the **Music** box asks every backend at once: a slow streaming extension slows it down (Gladys waits 10 seconds).
- The search queues at most 50 tracks, a playlist at most 500.
- Mopidy cannot be found automatically on the network: enter the addresses.
- The volume of the **Talk on a speaker** action is not passed on by Gladys
  (the **Notification volume** applies).
- Gladys 5.3.0 or later (the music player and its panels).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Mopidy asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Mopidy servers | `section` | No | Mopidy with its HTTP frontend (Mopidy-HTTP, port 6680), reachable from Gladys: set hostname = 0.0.0.0 in the [http] section of mopidy.conf. Enter its IP address (add :port if it is not 6680). Up to four servers. |
| Server address | `string` | No | IP address or name of the Mopidy server, with :port if it is not 6680. The address of its web client works too. |
| Name | `string` | No | Name of the device in Gladys. Empty: "Mopidy" followed by the address. |
| Second server | `section` | No | Same fields, for another Mopidy server of your network. |
| Server address | `string` | No |  |
| Name | `string` | No |  |
| Third server | `section` | No | Same fields, for another Mopidy server of your network. |
| Server address | `string` | No |  |
| Name | `string` | No |  |
| Fourth server | `section` | No | Same fields, for another Mopidy server of your network. |
| Server address | `string` | No |  |
| Name | `string` | No |  |
| Options | `section` | No | The notification of a server plays an address (a doorbell sound, an announcement), then puts back what was playing. |
| Notification volume | `select` | No | Volume during a notification, back to the previous one after. Gladys does not pass on the volume of its "Talk on a speaker" action. |
| Language of the devices | `select` | No | Names given to the features when a device is added (Volume, Playlist…), and language of the messages. |

## How to install Mopidy in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Mopidy appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-mopidy:1.1.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mopidy](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mopidy).

Mopidy requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Mopidy is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [guim31](https://github.com/guim31), not by the Gladys core team.
